flawed_step: The conclusion that stratum-wise dominance implies aggregate dominance is false (Simpson's paradox): the overall rate is a weighted average of stratum rates, and the weights P(C|T) and P(C|not-T) can differ.
counterexample: Uniform space of 22 points. T∧C: 1 point, 1 success (rate 1). ¬T∧C: 10 points, 9 successes (rate 0.9). T∧¬C: 10 points, 1 success (rate 0.1). ¬T∧¬C: 1 point, 0 successes (rate 0). All cells have positive probability; 1 > 0.9 and 0.1 > 0. But P(S|T) = 2/11 < 9/11 = P(S|¬T).
assessment_summary: Simpson's paradox. Explicit 22-point counterexample: the treatment does better within each stratum, but the treated group is mostly in the low-success stratum, so its overall success rate is lower (2/11 vs 9/11).
